strings: Stonewatch is a fortified stronghold in central Redridge Mountains, built to defend the surrounding human lands from northern invasions. Formerly manned by Stormwind soldiers, the fortress has fallen under the brutal control of the Blackrock orcs, posing an immediate threat to nearby Lakeshire.

Positioned over the cliffs near Stonewatch Falls, Stonewatch comprises a heavily built tower and keep designed to guard the approaches from the Burning Steppes. Originally held by Lakeshire's defenders, the fortification fell when the rogue warlock Morganth forged an alliance with the Blackrock clan. Infused with dark magic, the invading orcs overwhelmed the local human garrison—the 12th Sabre Regiment—and claimed the fortress. Although Morganth eventually turned on his allies and withdrew to the nearby Tower of Ilgalar with an army of Shadowhide gnolls, the Blackrock orcs retained a stranglehold over the keep under the command of General Gath'Ilzogg and Lieutenant Tharil'zun.

With Stonewatch firmly garrisoned by hostile orcs, Lakeshire sits directly in the crosshairs of an impending conquest. Cut off from substantial military reinforcements by an indifferent or paralyzed Stormwind House of Nobles, Magistrate Solomon and Marshal Marris have been forced to hire mercenary aid and volunteers. Decapitating the fortress's leadership—targeting both Tharil'zun and Gath'Ilzogg—remains the town's desperate primary hope for relieving the siege on the region.

Stonewatch Keep is a fortified stone stronghold looming in eastern Redridge Mountains, once built and manned by the Kingdom of Stormwind. It has fallen to an invading host of Blackrock orcs, serving as the forward operational base from which their warlords terrorize Lakeshire.

Stonewatch Keep originally defended the eastern ridges and guarded the settlers of Lakeshire against hostile incursions. That peace shattered when the renegade warlock Morganth struck an alliance with the Blackrock clan. Bolstered by dark magic, the orcs stormed the fortress with vicious ferocity, overwhelming the human defenders and taking the keep for themselves. Although Morganth later abandoned his allies to raise the nearby Tower of Ilgalar and subjugate local gnolls, the Blackrock invaders successfully consolidated their grip over Stonewatch, transforming a former bastion of the Alliance into a fortified staging ground for their assault on the valley.

Now occupied by a heavy garrison of Blackrock warriors, the keep is overseen by the formidable orcish warlord Gath'Ilzogg and his brutal lieutenant, Tharil'zun. From the stone ramparts, these commanders coordinate raids across Redridge, taking prisoners such as Stormwind's Corporal Keeshan. With the kingdom's military spread thin and unable to dispatch a full regiment to liberate the fortress, Magistrate Solomon and Marshal Marris have been forced to hire mercenary champions to infiltrate the stronghold and execute the Blackrock leadership before Lakeshire is completely overrun.

The Stonewrought Dam is a colossal dwarven engineering marvel standing along the northern rim of Loch Modan. It holds back the waters of the Loch, creating the massive highland lake while draining the Wetlands below into habitable marshes.

Stretching across the canyon east of Dun Algaz, the Stonewrought Dam is widely regarded as one of the great structural triumphs of dwarven civilization. Designed by the master Dark Iron architect Franclorn Forgewright, the barrier was built using his pioneering stonewrought technique. By trapping the waters of the mountain basin, the dam doubled the surface area of the Loch while steadily lowering water levels to the north, allowing the marshy basin of the Wetlands to emerge from a once completely flooded valley.

Though built under the guidance of a Dark Iron architect, the dam today serves Ironforge—and has become a prime target for Dark Iron saboteurs operating out of the southern mountains. Recent assaults and infiltration attempts have forced Ironforge to station a garrison here under Chief Engineer Hinderweir VII. Guards and engineers patrol the masonry day and night, knowing that any breach would catastrophically drain the Loch and unleash a devastating deluge across the Wetlands below.

The Stormrage Barrow Dens are an ancient subterranean sanctuary carved beneath the sacred valley of Moonglade. Named for Malfurion Stormrage, these quiet earth-hewn chambers serve as a dedicated resting place where druids enter long, restorative slumbers to wander the Emerald Dream.

Barrow dens serve as sacred havens throughout night elven lands, providing druids a safe subterranean refuge where their physical bodies can lie undisturbed during lengthy immersions in the Emerald Dream. The Stormrage Barrow Dens are particularly esteemed within the sacred realm of Moonglade. Named in honor of Archdruid Malfurion Stormrage, these winding earthen halls hold both ancient reverence and quiet vigil. While some druids like Clintar Dreamwalker still slumber safely within its alcoves, the absence of the great Archdruid himself casts a somber shadow over the hollowed roots and peaceful glowing lanterns.

During the desperate days of the Third War, these dens stood on the brink of total ruin. The dreadlord Tichondrius and the Burning Legion's forces sought to eradicate the sleeping druids before they could rally. High Priestess Tyrande Whisperwind fought her way through invading demons and hostile corrupted wildlife deep into these earthen tunnels to blow the Horn of Cenarius, waking Malfurion Stormrage in the nick of time. Following Archimonde's defeat at Mount Hyjal, Malfurion returned to Moonglade to commune with the spirits, but his essence has once more drifted into the Dream, leaving his brethren to watch over these sacred earthen depths.

Stormwind City is the majestic capital of the Kingdom of Stormwind and the military and political heart of the Alliance. Rebuilt from ashes following its destruction in the First War, it stands as the greatest remaining bastion of human power in Azeroth following the fall of the northern kingdoms.

Founded over a millennium ago by Arathi descendants migrating south, Stormwind flourished as a vibrant coastal capital ringed by stone ramparts and powered by swift rivermills. That grandeur ended in the First War when the Orcish Horde besieged the city, breached its defenses, and burned it to the ground, forcing Sir Anduin Lothar to lead surviving refugees across the Great Sea to Lordaeron. Following the victory of the Alliance in the Second War, the Stonemasons' Guild undertook the monumental task of rebuilding the capital into the gleaming fortress of white stone, canal networks, and towering spires that stands north of Elwynn Forest today.

With Lordaeron shattered by the Scourge and Dalaran heavily ruined during the Third War, Stormwind City serves as the primary refuge and stronghold for mankind. Its broad avenues and defensive walls are patrolled by the disciplined Stormwind City Guard, while the spires of the Cathedral of Light guide faith and devotion across the southern kingdoms. Yet beneath its orderly districts and ceremonial gates lies quiet political turmoil: King Varian Wrynn has mysteriously vanished, leaving his young son Anduin on the throne under the regency of Highlord Bolvar Fordragon and the whispered counsel of royal advisor Lady Katrana Prestor.

Tucked away beneath the canals along the northern edge of the Mage Quarter, the Stockade serves as Stormwind's high-security penitentiary. Intended to lock away murderers, political dissidents, and foreign enemies, the subterranean fortress has recently collapsed into total chaos following a coordinated inmate rebellion.

Ordinarily overseen by Warden Thelwater, the Stockade is where the kingdom deposits its most volatile prisoners, ranging from cutthroats and Defias operatives to captured Blackrock orcs and Dark Iron dwarves. However, a violent uprising orchestrated by the cunning Defias conspirator Bazil Thredd has entirely displaced the prison guards. The inmates now roam freely in the lower cells, turning the fortress into a fortress of riots. Thelwater, having barely secured the entry thresholds, relies on independent adventurers to plunge into the subterranean corridors and suppress the revolt before it spills out into the canals.

The Stockade holds more than ordinary street convicts; it has long served as a bargaining chip for the kingdom's corrupt House of Nobles. Murderers and high-value prisoners who received death sentences elsewhere—such as the graverobber Dextren Ward from Duskwood or the Blackrock warlord Targorr the Dread from Redridge—have had their executions delayed by aristocratic interference to serve as political pawns. Carved deep beneath the northern mountains of the Badlands, Uldaman is an ancient titan vault dating back to the ordering of the world. Recently unsealed by dwarven excavators, its halls contain the buried origins of the dwarven race alongside savage troggs and vigilant stone sentinels.
The Vault of the First Creations

Uldaman was constructed by titan watchers as a subterranean redoubt and research facility. When early experiments in shaping living stone produced the misshapen troggs, the titans sealed their failed creations within the vault's stasis chambers and began anew, culminating in the stone-skinned earthen. Its deepest chambers came to hold vital archives, including the fabled Discs of Norgannon, guarded by the stonekeeper Archaedas and the giantess Ironaya. In time the stone-skinned earthen gave rise to the dwarven race, and their cradle lay buried and forgotten beneath the hills.

When Ironforge prospectors broke through Uldaman's exterior gates, their pickaxes inadvertently cracked open the stasis chambers. Hordes of awakened troggs overran the upper tunnels, driving back dwarven teams and severing early dig sites. Compounding the chaos, Dark Iron dwarves marched into the ruins seeking artifacts of supreme power for their fiery master, Ragnaros. Today, the deep shafts remain a war ground between rival dig teams, bloodthirsty troggs, and titan constructs that awaken to smash any trespasser regardless of clan or cause.
